title_en: Great Wall Broadband Network Service Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch v. China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch — dispute over restoration to original condition
ruling_gist_en: Communication pipelines within a residential community belong to all owners collectively after the community is delivered. A clause in a contract between a telecom operator and the real estate development company of the community that grants the telecom operator exclusive usage rights over communication pipelines and other communication facilities within the community infringes upon the owners' collective ownership rights and their freedom to choose telecom services, and shall be invalid.

full_text_en:
Great Wall Broadband Network Service Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch v. China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch — dispute over restoration to original condition

【Ruling Summary】

Communication pipelines in a residential community shall belong to all owners of the community after the delivery of the community. Any clause in an agreement between a communication operator and the real estate development company of the community that grants the communication operator exclusive usage rights over communication facilities such as communication pipelines within the community infringes upon the common ownership rights of the owners and violates the freedom of choice of the owners to select telecommunication services, and shall be invalid.

Plaintiff: Great Wall Broadband Network Service Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, domiciled at Gaofeng Road, Jiangning District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Responsible Person: Li Yongqiang, General Manager of the Branch.
Defendant: China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch, domiciled at Jiangdong North Road, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Responsible Person: Wang Huiyan, General Manager of the Branch.

The plaintiff, Great Wall Broadband Network Service Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Company), instituted an action in the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch (hereinafter referred to as Tietong Nanjing Branch), concerning a dispute over restoration to original condition.

The plaintiff, Great Wall Company, alleged: On September 18, 2013, it entered into a "Community Broadband Internet Access Cooperative Operation Agreement" with Nanjing Qiantai Property Management Co., Ltd. Thereafter, it carried out cabling construction in the South Garden Community in accordance with the agreement. On September 27, 2014, its staff discovered that multiple optical cables (5,653 meters of 4-core optical cables and 1,056 meters of 48-core optical cables) laid by it in the aforementioned community had been cut, and 1,309 meters of twisted pair cables had been cut and taken away. Its staff called 110 to report the incident. After investigation by the Chalu Police Station of the Jiangning Branch of the Nanjing Public Security Bureau, it was confirmed that the optical cables and twisted pair cables had been cut by the staff of the defendant, Tietong Nanjing Branch. After unsuccessful mediation by the police station, the plaintiff requested the court to order Tietong Nanjing Branch to restore the cut optical cables and twisted pair cables to their original condition and to bear the case acceptance fee.

The defendant, Tietong Nanjing Branch, argued: In September 2014, during a routine inspection, its staff discovered some old and discarded cables of unknown ownership, which they then removed. There is no evidence confirming that the plaintiff, Great Wall Company, is the owner of the cables. Even if Great Wall Company were the owner, according to the "Jingwei Real Estate South Garden C Group Telephone Agreement" signed between China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch (hereinafter referred to as Tietong Jiangsu Branch) and Jiangsu Jingwei Real Estate Co., Ltd. on October 25, 2001, its company has exclusive usage rights over the outdoor pipelines and indoor line channels within the C Group of the South Garden Community, and Great Wall Company has no right to lay optical cables in its exclusive communication pipelines. In summary, the defendant requested the court to dismiss Great Wall Company's claims against it.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing found the following facts at the first instance:

1. On September 18, 2013, the plaintiff, Great Wall Company (Party A), and Nanjing Qiantai Property Management Co., Ltd. (Party B, hereinafter referred to as Qiantai Company) entered into a "Community Broadband Internet Access Business Cooperative Operation Agreement", stipulating: Party A and Party B shall jointly build a community broadband network in the South Garden Community; Party A shall bear the investment, design, construction, maintenance, and technical renovation of the network engineering construction of the information-based community, and shall provide internet broadband access services for the community; Party A has the right to use existing network lines and equipment within the community. Thereafter, Great Wall Company laid cables in the outdoor communication pipelines and indoor line channels of the South Garden Community.

2. In September 2014, staff of the defendant, Tietong Nanjing Branch, cut a total of 5,653 meters of 4-core optical cables, 1,056 meters of 48-core optical cables, and 1,309 meters of twisted pair cables laid by Great Wall Company in the C Group of the South Garden Community, and took away the twisted pair cables. After discovering that the cables had been cut and were missing, Great Wall Company staff reported the matter to the police on September 27, 2014, and the Chalu Police Station of the Jiangning Branch of the Nanjing Public Security Bureau responded.

3. Additionally, on June 26, 2011, Jiangsu Jingwei Real Estate Co., Ltd. (Party A, hereinafter referred to as Jingwei Company) and Qiantai Company (Party B) signed a "Preliminary Property Service Contract" with a term from July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2014, stipulating: Party A appoints Party B to provide preliminary property management services for the South Garden Community; Party B provides services including the repair and maintenance of common parts of the property and the daily operation and repair maintenance of common facilities and equipment of the property; Party B manages and operates the property belonging to all owners, and after deducting relevant operating expenses, the remaining income shall be used to subsidize property service fees. The aforementioned contract was stamped with the seal of the Owners' Committee of the C Group of the South Garden Community.

4. On October 25, 2001, China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch (Party B, formerly known as Telecommunication Information Co., Ltd. Jiangsu Branch) and Jingwei Company (Party A) signed the "Jingwei Real Estate South Garden C Group Telephone Agreement", stipulating: Party A agrees that Party B shall be the telephone business operator for the C Group of the South Garden Community, and Party B shall be responsible for the installation, maintenance, and operation of telephones in the community; Party A shall be responsible for the construction of outdoor pipelines and indoor line channels within the community, as well as the construction of indoor drop wires to the households, with costs borne by Party A. During the cooperation period, the right to use these facilities shall belong to Party B; Party B shall be responsible for the construction of equipment in the telephone exchange room and outdoor cables, with costs borne by Party B, and the property rights and usage rights shall belong to Party B; the cooperation period of the agreement is 20 years; during the cooperation period, Party A's South Garden Community C Group shall not cooperate with any other company for the same or similar services; if any party undergoes a change in ownership or management rights during the cooperation period, affecting the cooperation and operation of the project, the changing party shall notify the other party in writing sixty days before the change and transfer this agreement to the assignee of ownership or management rights to continue performing the terms of this agreement. On July 17, 2002, Tietong Nanjing Branch was established.

5. It was further found that Jingwei Company is the developer of the South Garden Community, which was developed and delivered in phases, with the last batch of houses in the C Group delivered in 2009.

During the trial, Tietong Jiangsu Branch issued a "Statement of Circumstances", stating: it had signed the "Jingwei Real Estate South Garden C Group Telephone Agreement" with Jingwei Company in October 2001; after the agreement was signed, Tietong Nanjing Branch was established, and it transferred its assets in the Nanjing area to Tietong Nanjing Branch, along with the rights and obligations under the related agreements.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing held at the first instance:

Property rights of legal persons are protected by law. The clause in the "Jingwei Real Estate South Garden C Group Telephone Agreement" signed between Tietong Jiangsu Branch and Jingwei Company, stipulating that Tietong Jiangsu Branch shall have exclusive use of the communication pipelines in the C Group of the South Garden Community for 20 years, restricts the access of other telecommunication operators to the C Group of the South Garden Community, undermines the market environment for fair competition, limits the right of community owners to freely choose telecommunication services, and harms the interests of community owners. Therefore, this clause is invalid. Consequently, the court does not accept the defendant Tietong Nanjing Branch's argument, based on the "Jingwei Real Estate South Garden C Group Telephone Agreement", that it enjoyed exclusive usage rights over the outdoor pipelines and indoor line channels in the C Group of the South Garden Community. According to the provisions of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, other public places, public facilities, and property service premises within the building area shall belong to the owners collectively. Communication pipelines within a community are a type of public facility, being one of the supporting facilities necessary for the developer to construct the community's buildings to meet the functional needs of the exclusive parts of the buildings. After the developer delivers the houses, the communication pipelines should belong to the owners collectively. After the delivery of the C Group of the South Garden Community, the communication pipelines within the community belonged to the owners of the C Group of the South Garden Community. Qiantai Company provides preliminary property services for all owners of the community, including the repair and maintenance of common parts of the property, the daily operation and repair maintenance of common facilities and equipment, and the management and operation of the property belonging to all owners. Qiantai Company has the right to dispose of the communication pipelines owned collectively by the owners. The plaintiff, Great Wall Company, based on the "Community Broadband Internet Access Cooperative Operation Agreement" signed with Qiantai Company, has the right to lay cables in the communication pipelines of the South Garden Community. After discovering cables not belonging to its company in the communication pipelines, Tietong Nanjing Branch, without ascertaining the ownership of the cables, unilaterally cut the cables and removed some of them, thereby infringing upon Great Wall Company's property rights and should bear tort liability. Great Wall Company's request for restoration to the original condition is legally grounded, and the court supports it.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 73 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 6 and 15 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 52, item (4) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing rendered the following judgment on May 7, 2015: The defendant, China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch, shall, within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, restore to their original condition the cables that it cut and removed from the plaintiff, Great Wall Broadband Network Service Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch; if the defendant, China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch, fails to restore them within the aforementioned period, the plaintiff, Great Wall Broadband Network Service Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, may restore them itself, with the cost of restoration borne by the defendant, China Tietong Group Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period, and the judgment has become legally effective.
